title: WHAT THE DATA SAY: Third of Americans feel they’re more likely to die from AI than old age
body_markdown:
By: Ray Day


## **CONTACT:**


Ray Day
ray.day@stagwellglobal.com


*We wanted to share our latest consumer and business insights, based on research from[Stagwell](https://www.stagwellglobal.com/) and[Allison Worldwide](https://www.allisonworldwide.com/) .* *Among the highlights of our weekly* *consumer sentiment tracking:*


**AI REVOLT**


Americans are wary of AI’s risks and increasingly reliant on it – especially Gen Z, who is using AI for work and emotional support, according to a new report from[The Harris Poll](https://www.canva.com/design/DAHTZvBy23M/5GGG7fu0WIjTw4A3goPDIg/view?utm_content=DAHTZvBy23M&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=uniquelinks&utlId=he94ec91358) .


- 28% of Americans (and 38% of Gen Z) believe they are more likely to die from AI than from old age.
- 53% oppose data centers locally, and 38% of Gen Z has protested or spoken out against one (compared with 26% of the general population).
- While 68% say AI can be useful, the same number says AI feels forced on them.
- 48% of Gen Z has avoided a brand because it uses AI, while 52% have actively tried to use AI less.
- At the same time, 54% of Gen Z and Millennials say AI has become so useful that they could not easily return to life without it.
- 53% of Gen Z and Millennials use AI for emotional support or companionship each month.
- 54% talk to AI rather than a person when they need support.
- Among those turning to AI for support, 57% say it feels safer, 47% say it is less expensive, and 31% say it is cheaper than seeing a professional.
- *See also:[A quarter of Americans would consider an AI partner if they were alone in 20 years](https://theharrispoll.com/articles/america-this-week-september-17-2026/)* ****


**THE RETIREMENT SQUEEZE**


Retirement is looking less certain and more expensive for Americans due to inflation and Social Security uncertainty, according to new Harris Poll research with[Athene](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/harris-poll-finds-gen-x-120000209.html) .


- 83% of Americans say their generation faces retirement challenges previous generations did not.
- 61% say they have fewer guaranteed retirement-income options than prior generations.
- 63% are concerned Social Security will run out of funds before they can collect benefits.
- 67% cite rising health care costs as their leading retirement concern, followed by inflation (62%).
- Half of respondents say inflation is affecting their ability to save for retirement, and day-to-day expenses also are eroding retirement preparedness for 39% of Americans.
- *See also:[Half of Current GLP-1 Users Say They May Have to Choose Between Medication and Retirement Savings](https://news.nationwide.com/half-of-current-glp-1-users-say-they-may-have-to-choose-between-medication-and-retirement-savings/)*


**CRYPTO CURIOUS**


Most Americans who do not own crypto are open to it, yet they need more trusted guidance before buying, according to[The 2026 Crypto Readiness Report](https://nca.org/2026%20Crypto%20Readiness%20Report.pdf) from Harris Poll and the National Cryptocurrency Association.


- 59% of non-holders are open to crypto, including 7% who expect to buy soon.
- More than 33 million Americans who do not currently own crypto say they are likely to buy.
- 55% of likely buyers are people of color, 43% are women and 42% have household incomes below $75,000.
- Lack of understanding is the top ownership barrier (48%), followed by security and fraud concerns (43%) and those who say crypto is a scam (13%).
